subject: Streaming fallback observed — EmberTech app impacted
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming fallback observed — EmberTech app impacted

Hi Sarah,

Wanted to let you know we detected increased streaming stalls for your EmberChat stream between 08:45–09:05 PDT this morning. Traffic hit an unusual prefix cache eviction pattern, which caused a portion of requests to route to a lower-capacity fallback model for ~12 minutes. Customers using streaming saw partial responses or truncated completions while we applied mitigation.

What we did: 
- Automatically routed affected requests to a high-availability fallback pool to preserve throughput (this reduced output length/quality in a subset of completions).
- Applied a hotfix to reduce KV eviction aggression and re-warm common prefixes.
- Cleared a backlog; streaming resumed to normal p95 within ~30m of detection.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-08-04-embertech (live incident entry with timeline).
Attachments: incident_snapshot.log, timeline.csv (short traces and per-region token counts).

Next steps: we will follow up with a short post-incident summary and recommended configuration changes to avoid re-triggering (prefetch/cache settings and a suggested canary for model variants). Expect our next update by 15:00 PDT.

Apologies for the disruption — we know EmberChat depends on consistent streaming. If you saw specific failures or have examples (request IDs), send them over and we'll prioritize those traces.

—Kim
Kimberly Park

Kim, Grace — quick internal summary and ask for ops traces (internal thread):

Observed behavior: KV cache churn in us-west-2 caused >30% of active hot prefixes to be evicted during a short memory pressure event. Our routing policy considered hot prefixes cold and selected a lower-capacity variant with smaller KV footprint which reinstated throughput but reduced context window per-stream.
Impact: ~12 minutes of higher truncation rate for EmberTech (they reported truncated streams). No customer payloads were persisted beyond normal logging; we did not reprocess user payloads.
Action items:
- Operations: please attach the kube/node memory events, model variant switch logs, and the streaming p95/p99 traces for 08:40–09:10 PDT.
- Product: propose a quick config change to prefetch common prefixes for EmberTech edge pools and to reduce automatic fallback sensitivity.
- Accounts: coordinate EmberTech credit offer and external comms.

Do not forward this internal summary to external recipients; I will compose the formal post-incident notice once we have the traces.

—Aditya

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2026-08-04 EmberTech streaming disruption

Hi Sarah,

Thank you for your patience while we completed the initial investigation. Below is a short summary and the items we promised.

Executive summary (what happened)
- Between 08:45–08:57 PDT we observed memory pressure in the us-west-2 serving pool that caused frequent KV cache evictions. This triggered our routing policy to move a fraction of requests to a smaller-model variant to maintain availability. The smaller variant has a reduced context window which caused truncated streaming output for some sessions.

Root cause (technical)
- A recently deployed autoscaler tuning change increased background preemption of cache-backed worker pods under spike conditions. This reduced effective KV cache residency for hot prefixes and increased eviction churn.

Actions taken
- Rolled back the autoscaler tweak and rebalanced pool allocations (08:57–09:05 PDT).
- Implemented a short-term prefetch for EmberTech hot prefixes and increased the eviction threshold for the us-west-2 pool.
- Ops: added alerting to detect similar cache-churn patterns earlier.

Customer impact and data handling
- Impact window: 08:45–09:05 PDT. During that window some streams experienced truncation or reduced completion length. We confirmed no user payloads were reprocessed beyond normal ephemeral logging.

Remediation and mitigation plan
- Product will ship a guarded autoscaler config that avoids aggressive preemption for customers with >150 concurrent streaming sessions (ETA: 2 weeks).
- We recommend EmberTech adopt the prefetch setting we applied as a permanent config in your dedicated routing policy; we can push this as a rollout starting next week.

Compensation
- As a gesture for the disruption, we will apply a one-time 25% service credit for the impacted usage window. Accounts team will follow up with a formal credit memo.

Links and artifacts
- Live status entry: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-08-04-embertech
- Post-incident write-up (PDF): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/postmortems/embertech-2026-08-04
- Attached: postmortem-summary.pdf (brief timeline, root cause, and action plan).

If you want a short sync to walk through the postmortem or to review the prefetch rollout plan, I can set aside 30 minutes tomorrow. Please let me know what time works.

Thanks again and very sorry for the interruption.

—Kim
